description:
Refactor the PR #847 disable flow to extend the shared path already on main, removing the separate WhatsApp disable route and its dedicated tests. Requested by the user after reviewing the original listener teardown and optional adapter logout callback. Planning only; this request does not start implementation.

Agreed contract: BO requests disable and displays any required confirmation. Channels resolves the configured adapter and performs optional logout synchronously while the persisted connector is still enabled, preserving credential access. Logout failure returns an error and prevents successful disable/persistence. After successful logout, or when unsupported, Engine persists enabled: false and Channels performs the existing listener/runtime teardown. Delete reuses this operation before archival. BO and Engine must not branch on WhatsApp or invoke adapter logout themselves. Authorization remains application-owned. Runtime-stop failure after persistence remains an explicit retryable outcome; remote logout cannot be rolled back if later persistence fails.

Baseline audited: local main a2a1a1e9e has ChannelsLive.toggle_active_config/sync_channel_runtime, Channels :sync_channel_runtime, bridge sync/stop, ConnectorLifecycle.archive and ConnectorRuntime reconciliation. Dedicated DisableChannelConnector, connector_logout routing and logout integration are PR additions. Original listener stop is JidoChatBridge.sync_runtime enabled->disabled calling stop_runtime; webhook teardown is a separate subsequent operation. Main persists disabled before sync, so merely inserting logout before stop_runtime is insufficient. Extend the shared operation across the existing Engine persistence / Channels runtime boundary; do not preserve two disable implementations under renamed wrappers.

Scope: shared disable, Delete integration, remove obsolete disable Action/API/helpers and dedicated tests after reference audit; preserve shared enable/archive code. Other findings in WHATSAPP_ADAPTER_BOUNDARY_FINDINGS.md are not automatically in scope. No stopping field/controller, NodeRouter coordination or AsyncHandoff. Preserve existing operator authorization, exact selected profile, revision checks, non-logout adapter behavior and webhook teardown. Missing listener must have an explicit cleanup/result contract; clearing local credentials must not be represented as confirmed remote unlinking.

User explicitly authorizes removal of tests tied to the discarded disable route. Move necessary behavior coverage to the shared path before removing those tests; do not discard authorization, failure ordering or profile isolation assertions. Other behavioral changes still follow docs/testing-approach.md.

Action reuse: extend the existing shared toggle/runtime and archive domain operations; optional adapter invocation is a Channels-local implementation detail. No new agent tool or standalone logout Action. BO cross-service calls use confidential NodeRouter events; Engine retains persistence. Existing Actions/tools/workflow callers must be audited before removing entry points.

Delivery: linear dependency chain of five child tasks; tests and docs attached to each implementation step. Existing LiveView/integration coverage is appropriate for this internal refactor with unchanged UX; no new feature E2E planned. Reassess and obtain the handbook UX gate if scope introduces a new browser journey. Validation follows docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md; final review and post-review coverage handoff are explicit tasks. Prior epic zaq-mvw removed coordination and withdrew its stopping implementation; do not revive that contract.

comments.text: Dependency chain: zaq-ojt.1 -> zaq-ojt.2 -> zaq-ojt.3 -> zaq-ojt.4 -> zaq-ojt.5. User requested planning and explicit removal of tests related to the discarded disable route. Preserve behavior coverage on the shared operation. Other provider-boundary findings remain outside this epic unless needed for disable integration.

Implementation detail from baseline audit: BO main toggle persists directly before runtime sync. Extend existing sync_channel_runtime event with an ID-scoped requested enabled transition, using Channels to prepare optional bridge logout, existing confidential connector_lifecycle Engine command for generic canonical read/revision-checked persistence, then existing runtime sync. Keep old before/after runtime-only events compatible. No new disable event or standalone Action. Archive uses same transition with existing runtime-stop leaf to avoid repeating webhook deletion. All states remain existing enabled/archive fields.

Implementation tasks 1-4 completed in working tree. Actual flow: BO shared sync_channel_runtime request -> Channels canonical snapshot and optional synchronous before_disable adapter logout -> Engine revision-checked disabled persistence -> original Channels runtime teardown. Same transition used by Delete before archive. No persistent stopping state or router coordination. Dedicated route tests removed; meaningful behavior retained in shared preparation/transition/integration suites. Final focused result: 366 passed, mix q passed. Remaining .5 tracks review approval, post-review coverage and final gate.

title: [zaq-ojt] Consolidate connector disable into the shared adapter-aware path
